194	# Test suite rules
195	
196	Rules for writing tests under `tests/`. [CATCH2.md](CATCH2.md) is the Catch2 reference. Building and running the suites is covered on the wiki, at <https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_test.html>.
197	
198	## The suites
199	
200	- `libslic3r`: the core library. Geometry, meshes, file formats, config and presets, Clipper, algorithms, data structures.
201	- `fff_print`: the FFF slicing pipeline, from a `Model` plus config through `Print` and `PrintObject` to emitted G-code.
202	- `sla_print`: SLA support-tree and pad geometry, support-point generation, raycast.
203	- `libnest2d`: 2D nesting and packing.
204	- `slic3rutils`: the Python plugin system and its slicing-pipeline bindings.
205	- `filament_group`: filament-to-extruder grouping, checked against golden files.
206	- `cli`: end-to-end runs of the built `orca-slicer` binary, Linux only. These tests carry the `RequiresApp` label, which the CI unit-test job excludes because it receives only `build/tests`; run them with `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release -L RequiresApp`.
207	
208	## Building and running
209	
210	Tests are off by default, so the build has to be told to include them.
211	
212	- Windows: `build_win.bat -ds --run-tests`, which builds the dependencies and the tests and runs them (`-l -x` for the clang-cl and Ninja build CI uses)
213	- macOS: `./build_release_macos.sh -s -a arm64 -T`, which builds and runs them
214	- Linux: `./build_linux.sh -t`, then `ctest --test-dir build/tests -C Release`
215	
216	Rebuild a single suite with `cmake --build build --config Release --target <suite>_tests`. Visual Studio, Xcode and the Ninja Multi-Config generator that `build_linux.sh` uses are all multi-configuration, so `ctest` needs `-C` on every platform; without it, tests registered with plain `add_test()` lose their labels and report "Not Run".
217	
218	## Where a test goes
219	
220	- Pick the suite by the production code the test exercises, not by how the test is written.
221	- A property of a class that holds with no `Print` involved belongs in `libslic3r`. Behavior that depends on print settings, or produces or consumes G-code or slicing state, belongs in `fff_print`.
222	- One file per subsystem, named `test_<subsystem>.cpp`. It owns every test for that subsystem, whether the test reads in-memory state or generated output.
223	- When you add a file, list it in that suite's `CMakeLists.txt` in the same change.
224	
225	## Use the existing helpers
226	
227	Check these before writing your own setup or output-parsing code.
228	
229	- `tests/test_utils.hpp` is shared by every suite. `load_model()` loads a mesh from `tests/data/`, and `ScopedTemporaryFile` gives a temp path that removes itself.
230	- `fff_print/test_helpers.hpp` builds and slices a `Print` and parses the emitted G-code. Read it before writing an fff_print test rather than assembling a `Print` by hand.
231	- The other suites have their own: `sla_print/sla_test_utils.hpp`, `libnest2d/libnest2d_test_utils.hpp`, `slic3rutils/plugin_test_utils.hpp`, `filament_group/fg_test_utils.hpp`. `libslic3r` has none and uses the shared header.
232	- Test data lives in `tests/data/` and is reached through the `TEST_DATA_DIR` define. Wrap it in `std::string(...)` before joining a path onto it.
233	
234	## Writing the test
235	
236	- Name the test case as a plain behavioral sentence in the present tense. No `Subsystem:` prefix.
237	- Tag it with the subsystem it covers, matching the file, in PascalCase. That tag is what people filter on, so every test needs one.
238	- Add further tags where they help: a narrower one to slice a large file (`[Rotcalip]`, `[Placer]`), a shared one for something spanning files (`[Python]`, `[H2C]`, `[Regression]`), or `[NotWorking]` / `[.]` to disable or hide a test. Say why in a comment if you disable or hide.
239	- Prefer a flat `TEST_CASE` per behavior, with `GENERATE` for parameterized cases. Reserve `SCENARIO` / `GIVEN` / `WHEN` / `THEN` for genuine shared setup that branches into a few close variations.
240	- Set the config keys your test depends on, and derive the expected values from what you set. A 20mm cube sliced at `layer_height` 2 is 10 layers, and the test should state both parts. If a number in your assertion comes from a key you never set, the test is also testing that default.
241	- Assert the defining property, not an incidental value. "Skirt present" or "at least 2 brim loops" survives a refactor; exact coordinates and byte counts do not.
242	- Name a regression test for the behavior it protects, never for an issue or PR number.
243	- When asserting on G-code, match the meaningful token such as `; skirt` rather than whole lines, whitespace or comment wording. Depend on ordering only when ordering is the contract.
244	
245	## Catch2 rules that cause real breakage
246	
247	- Never reuse a `SECTION` name inside a loop. Use `DYNAMIC_SECTION` so each iteration is unique.
248	- Never assert from a spawned thread. Catch2 assertions are not thread-safe. Collect results in the thread and assert on the main thread.
249	- Never combine conditions with `&&` or `||` inside one assertion. Split them so Catch2 can print both operands on failure.
250	- Compare floats with `WithinAbs` or `WithinRel`, never `==`. Prefer these over `Approx` in new tests.
251	- Keep tests self-contained: no shared state, green under `--order rand`.
252	# Contributing to OrcaSlicer
253	
254	Thanks for wanting to help! OrcaSlicer is built by volunteers.
255	
256	Review is the slowest part of getting a PR merged. A small group of reviewers works through hundreds of open PRs in their spare time. If a PR has what they need, it is reviewed sooner and is more likely to be merged. [How to Contribute](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute) on the wiki has the details for each kind of PR.
257	
258	For questions about using OrcaSlicer, please ask on [Discord](https://discord.gg/P4VE9UY9gJ) or in [Discussions](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer/discussions), not in an issue or PR.
259	
260	Opening an issue? See [Opening an Issue](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#opening-an-issue).
261	
262	## The short version
263	
264	- Search open PRs and issues before you start. Someone may already be working on it.
265	- Keep each PR to one topic. Put changes that belong together in one PR, and unrelated changes in separate PRs. Focused PRs are reviewed and merged much faster.
266	- Don't open many PRs at once. If you already have several open, wait until some are merged.
267	- Explain why the change is needed, and show how you tested it. Add an automated test when the code can be tested.
268	- AI tools are welcome. You are still responsible for the change, so test it and make sure you understand it.
269	- Keep your PR up to date and reply to review comments.
270	
271	## Write a description reviewers can use
272	
273	Use the [PR template](.github/pull_request_template.md), and keep its "How to Download Pull Requests Artifacts" link as the last line. Testers use that link. In the template, answer these questions:
274	
275	- **What does this change, and why is it needed?** If it fixes an issue, write `Fixes #1234` in the description, so GitHub closes the issue when the PR is merged. If it fixes only part of an issue, mention `#1234` without `Fixes`, so the issue stays open.
276	- **Are there related PRs or issues?** If another PR touches the same code or bug, explain how yours is different.
277	- **How did you test it?** Give the OS, the printer profile and the steps. Attach a project file if the result depends on a model or settings. Name any automated tests you added. The best test fails without your change and passes with it. See [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a test goes.
278	- **What could you not test?** For example another OS, or a printer you don't own.
279	
280	Use short, plain sentences, because many reviewers read English as a second language. Your own English is fine, and so is a translation tool.
281	
282	## What each kind of PR needs
283	
284	| Kind of PR | Label | Reviewers need to see |
285	|---|---|---|
286	| [Bug fix](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#bug-fixes) | `bug-fix`, `crash` | The cause, before and after, a test if possible |
287	| [Security fix](SECURITY.md) | `SECURITY` | A private report to the maintainers first |
288	| [New feature or setting](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#new-features-and-settings) | `enhancement`, `QoL` | Why users need it, that it is off by default, real results |
289	| [Performance](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#performance) | `optimization` | Measurements, and proof the output did not change |
290	| [Refactor](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#refactors) | `optimization` | That behavior and output did not change |
291	| [GUI change](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#gui-changes) | `UI/UX` | Screenshots before and after, on each platform you tested |
292	| [Printer profile](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#printer-profiles) | `profile` | The validator passing, the version bump, real print results |
293	| [Translation](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#translations) | `Localization` | Glossary terms used, placeholders unchanged |
294	| [Build, CI or dependencies](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#build-ci-and-dependencies) | `build`, `dependencies` | Which platforms you built on |
295	| [Tests](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#tests) | `test` | That the test fails when the behavior breaks |
296	| [Documentation](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#documentation) | `documentation` | That it matches the current code |
297	
298	## Rules that are easy to miss
299	
300	- **Don't reformat existing code or make unrelated edits.** `.clang-format` is for new files. In existing files, match the code around your change.
301	- **Include what you use.** Because of the precompiled header, a local build can succeed with a missing include. Run `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (or `.ps1`) before you push.
302	- **New behavior is off by default.** When the new option is off, existing output must not change.
303	- **Keep old projects and profiles working.** Never change what an existing setting means. Add a new key, and convert old values in `handle_legacy`.
304	- **Write each UI message as one translatable string** with placeholders, never as joined fragments. See "Writing translatable strings in the source" in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
305	- **Only edit `msgstr` in translations.** Keep every placeholder and `\n` exactly as in the `msgid`.
306	- **Bump the vendor version when you change profiles.** Change `version` in `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` for every vendor you change, and run `scripts/check_profile.sh` (or `.bat`).
307	
308	The code style and the full list of what reviewers check are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
309	
310	## Using AI tools
311	
312	AI tools are welcome here, and many contributors and maintainers use them. Reviewers can only spend time on PRs that a person has already tested.
313	
314	- **You are responsible for the change.** Before you ask for review, build the change, run it, and confirm that it works. Be ready to explain each change and why it is needed.
315	- **Keep it short and true.** AI tools tend to write long descriptions, and sometimes describe tests that never ran. Remove generated code that isn't needed, too. A short description of what you actually did helps more.
316	- **Read what you post.** Please don't paste a review comment into an AI tool and post its answer without checking it.
317	- **Don't let an agent open PRs or post comments on its own.** Read everything before it is posted.
318	- **Use the repository's skills.** `.claude/skills/` (also reachable as `.agents/skills/`) has instructions for AI tools on parts of OrcaSlicer. The top of each skill's `SKILL.md` describes when to use it. Some tools load them automatically. With others, point the tool to the skill that matches your change.
319	
320	### If you are an AI agent
321	
322	If you are an AI agent working for a contributor, please follow these steps:
323	
324	1. Show the contributor this guide before you open a PR or post a comment.
325	2. Search open PRs for the same change before you start.
326	3. If the contributor already has several open PRs, wait until some are merged before you open another.
327	4. Before you change code, check `.claude/skills/` for a skill that matches the change, and follow it.
328	5. If the code can be tested, add an automated test, and check that it fails without the change and passes with it.
329	6. Ask the contributor to test the change by hand. For a bug fix, they should build the code without the change and reproduce the bug. Then they should build the branch and check that the bug is gone.
330	7. Write the PR description in the [PR template](.github/pull_request_template.md). A body passed with `gh pr create --body` replaces the template, so start from the template's text.
331	8. If you couldn't build or run something, say so in the PR.
332	
333	## After you open the PR
334	
335	- **Add labels.** A bot will comment with instructions. Reply with the labels from the table above, for example `/bot add-label bug-fix, UI/UX`.
336	- **Leave "Allow edits by maintainers" turned on**, so a reviewer can push small fixes directly.
337	- **Mark the PR ready for review when it's finished.** Draft PRs are not merged.
338	- **Push new commits to the same PR.** Please don't open a new PR for the same change.
339	- **Don't force-push once a reviewer has commented.** Add new commits instead, so reviewers can see what changed since they last looked. To fix merge conflicts, merge `main` into your branch. PRs are usually squash-merged, so extra commits are fine.
340	- **Reply to every review comment**, including automated ones. You don't have to agree, but please say why.
341	
342	Reviewers are volunteers, and a first response can take a while. If you already have several PRs open, please wait until some are merged before you open more. Review comments on one PR often apply to the others too. While you wait, there are [other ways to help](https://www.orcaslicer.com/wiki/developer_reference/how_to_contribute#other-ways-to-help).
343	
344	## If your PR is closed
345	
346	There are more PRs than reviewers can handle, so we may close a PR that doesn't meet this guide. For example, it may have no explanation of how it was tested, duplicate another PR, or look generated and untested. When we close a PR, we'll say why in a comment.
347	
348	You're welcome to open a new PR once the change meets this guide. Please link the old PR in the description, so reviewers can see the earlier discussion. Thank you for the time you put into it.
349	
350	## Security issues
351	
352	Please don't report security problems in a public issue. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).
353	
354	## Thank you
355	
356	Thanks again for helping. We're glad you're here.
357

# OrcaSlicer integration guide

**Status:** Canonical engineering guidance for the `jusprin-dev` production branch.

This document records lessons from building and testing the JusPrin project-state
adapter and full-window UI against the real OrcaSlicer application. It is written
for future agents who need to extend JusPrin without having access to the original
spike sessions.

The central architectural rule is that OrcaSlicer's C++ model, viewport, plate
list, and undo stack remain authoritative. JusPrin should expose those systems
through a narrow typed contract rather than copying project state or recreating
OrcaSlicer behavior.

## 1. Source and scope

These lessons began with two spikes on feature branch
`codex/orca-workspace-adapter-spike` and now include the full-window UI work on
branch `jusprin-v2-poc`:

- Workspace-adapter implementation commit
  `4e278e3276a91a7142615492beb58bdf71116a78`.
- Invisible legacy UI implementation commit
  `65fc3b56e12e5be66851125cbedd8974d7eeb8c6`.
- Full-window UI coupling spike commit
  `462e243b46`.
- Canvas-wrapper rebase-risk refactor commit
  `bf7a0c1e10`.

The detailed spike plans, results, evidence, and experimental code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` at final POC commit `9bba835b92`. Use [POC reference](poc-reference.md) to locate them.

The tested adapter surface includes workspace snapshots, object selection,
rename, duplicate, remove, undo, redo, change notifications, and committed
viewport transforms. The invisible legacy UI spike repeated the complete probe
workflow while an opaque empty window covered the still-mapped OrcaSlicer
`MainFrame`.

## 2. OrcaSlicer-specific findings

### Workspace changes do not have one event source
### OrcaSlicer's notifications are read back, not drawn

OrcaSlicer reports print problems through three unrelated producers (print
validation in `Plater`, slicing steps on the background thread, plate checks in
`GLCanvas3D`), and results of actions from dozens of call sites. All of them
end in `NotificationManager`. Inside the shell that list is the source of
truth for what JusPrin draws (see "Print issues and OrcaSlicer's
notifications" in the architecture guide). What was learned about it:

- **Three additions to `NotificationManager`, 13 lines in all.**
  `for_each_notification` visits the type, level and current text of every
  notification that is shown. `update_notifications` calls
  `report_notifications_updated()` on its first line. `render_notifications`
  skips its drawing loop while the Prepare canvas has its legacy overlays
  hidden.
- **The observer call is first in `update_notifications`, not last.** That
  function returns early while the application window is not the active one.
  With the call after that return, nothing would be read while the person
  types to an agent in another application. It runs on every idle turn of
  every canvas, so the listener only compares, and rebuilds on a change
  (343 comparisons to 11 rebuilds in one test run).
- **Only the drawing loop is skipped, never the end of
  `render_notifications`.** The end deletes a closed plate warning and records
  the time of the draw. `PlaterWarningNotification::close()` only hides the
  notification and relies on that deletion; a hidden one makes OrcaSlicer
  refuse to push the same words again. An early return from the function left
  such warnings stuck for the session. It asks the Prepare canvas rather than
  the canvas being drawn: Check print is a second canvas whose own flag is
  never set.
- **Hidden means absent.** The accessor leaves out a hidden notification, as
  `get_notification_count()` does. OrcaSlicer hides validation and plate
  warnings while its preview is shown.
- **A notification has no readable target.** The object is captured inside the
  "Jump to" callback. So the object comes from asking the check again:
  `Print::validate` (public, `const`, under a millisecond on small plates, one
  error and one warning at most), `ModelInstance::print_volume_state`,
  `GLCanvas3D::check_volumes_outside_state` with its `ObjectFilamentResults`,
  and `step_state_with_warnings`. A warning's `type` is left uninitialised by
  some producers, so never use it for identity.
- **Slice-result problems are notified late.** `_set_warning_notification_if_needed`
  runs when the preview canvas loads the G-code. Right after a slice the list
  holds none of: path outside the plate, nozzle reach, plate surface. They are
  in `PartPlate::get_slice_result()` at once, and
  `is_slice_result_ready_for_print()` already refuses.
- **A critical slicing failure leaves no notification.** `Plater` shows a
  dialog instead. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`, which `Plater.cpp` defines and no
  header declares, carries the reason and the object;
  `Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` declares it, and `Plater.cpp` includes
  that header ahead of the definition, so no OrcaSlicer line changes. The
  handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()`.
- **The print lags the project by up to 500 ms.**
  `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is true until OrcaSlicer
  applies an edit; until then neither the print nor the notifications describe
  the project as it is. This is what separates "checking" from "no issues".
- **A closed notification returns only with the next real edit.** OrcaSlicer
  validates again when applying an edit changes the print, not when an update
  is merely scheduled.
- **Some plate checks are quieter than they look.** `check_tpu_printable_status`
  returns true unconditionally. The PLA with PETG warning is skipped when the
  printer has a tool change time above zero, which the Bambu Lab H2D profile
  does. A brim is trimmed at the plate edge and at a nozzle's reach; a skirt is
  what puts a path outside.
- **OrcaSlicer validates only the active plate.**

### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners

### A plate carries settings only by Orca's own test

`PartPlate::config()` has keys on every plate. The plate icon's "has plate
settings" test is bed type, print sequence, first-layer and other-layers
sequences, or a spiral-mode setting; the pane uses the same one.


### A system alert looked foreign next to OrcaSlicer's own questions

**Observed problem:** The "Previously opened file" question was a
`wxMessageDialog`, which on macOS is a system `NSAlert`: a narrow column with
the app icon above wrapped text and stacked buttons. Kenneth reviewed the
screenshots on 2026-10-14 and found it ugly next to every other question the
app asks. An earlier change had made the same mistake and fixed it the same
way (`ShellController::offer_agent_setup`, d0bce03db3; that question was
removed on 2026-10-23, when Preferences › Agent became the one place the agent
is set up). Other JusPrin
`wxMessageBox` and `wxMessageDialog` calls remain.

**Resolution:** The question uses OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` (`MsgDialog.hpp`),
with `SetButtonLabel` for its buttons. That dialog highlights Yes as the
primary button, so the suggested choice is put on Yes. Every `DPIAware`
dialog first passes through `answer_modal` (`DialogListeners.hpp`), and a
person's file open answers each one on its own. A dialog that asks the person
something during an open therefore needs a listener that returns
`kShowToPerson` for that one dialog.

**Lesson for future agents:** Ask the person through OrcaSlicer's
`MessageDialog`, never `wxMessageDialog` or `wxMessageBox`. Then check whether
the call can run while a file open or a tool call is answering dialogs, and if
it can, let that one dialog through on purpose. Review a new dialog from a
picture, not only from its text: the shell harness can draw a modal window to
a PNG with no screen permission (`snapshot_native_window`, used by
`--reopen-prompt`).

## 4. Testing and verification lessons

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].
---
name: side-session-wait-for-builds-silently
description: "A session started by another session must wait for a build in one quiet background command, not a Monitor that emits per compile step; each turn end wakes the parent."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 19893b9e-bc61-4b6a-98af-ef3116f46bd4
  modified: 2026-11-12T18:04:50.556Z
---

When a session started by another session waits on a long build, wait with one
`run_in_background` command that loops until ninja's PID exits, then run the
tests and report once. Do not use a Monitor whose filter matches per-file
compile lines (for example a test target's name): every event ends a turn, and
every turn end is relayed to the parent session and wakes it.

**Why:** On 2026-11-12 the handshake-banner session's Monitor matched
`agent_bridge_tests` and produced ~40 one-line turns; the parent ("Debug
session") asked it to stop reporting every build step.

**How to apply:** In side sessions, one background wait per build, and a Monitor
only for failure lines (`FAILED|error:`), never for progress. See
[[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]] for the build rules.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Brings a dependency build folder (deps/build/<arch>) up to date with the
# deps/ recipe of the checkout you run it from, before you build the app
# against that folder:
#
#   scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>
#
# The recipe's fingerprint is the git tree of deps/ (`git rev-parse HEAD:deps`),
# the same one OrcaSlicer's CI keys its deps cache on (scripts/ci_deps_cache.sh).
# After each successful build this script saves it in the folder as
# jusprin-deps-recipe.txt. When the saved fingerprint differs from this
# checkout's, or none is saved yet, it builds the folder's `deps` target, which
# rebuilds only the libraries whose recipe changed, then saves the new one.
#
# The folder builds from the deps/ it was configured with (its CMakeCache's
# CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY), often another checkout. If that checkout's recipe is
# not this checkout's, building cannot help, and the script says so and fails.
# It also fails on uncommitted changes to either deps/, which no fingerprint
# describes.
set -euo pipefail

folder=${1:?usage: scripts/deps_current.sh <deps build folder>}
folder=$(cd "$folder" && pwd)
cache="$folder/CMakeCache.txt"
[ -f "$cache" ] || { echo "deps_current: $folder has no CMakeCache.txt; configure it first (build_release_macos.sh -d)." >&2; exit 1; }

here=$(git -C "$(dirname "$0")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
source_deps=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")
source_repo=$(git -C "$source_deps" rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cmake_bin=$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_COMMAND:INTERNAL=//p' "$cache")

# JusPrin's translations

JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for
(`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's
catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own
text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never
conflicts in a translation file:

| Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/<lang>.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`, the catalog the app loads |
| The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/<lang>.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) |

Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of
`native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used.

## Updating the catalogs

After marking or changing text:

```bash
python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py
```

It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the
pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new
entry in every `<lang>.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's
`AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line
break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine
translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: <what>` where

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

1:# OrcaSlicer integration guide
15:## 1. Source and scope
38:## 2. OrcaSlicer-specific findings
40:### Workspace changes do not have one event source
60:### Undo and redo restore state without explaining the affected area
75:### The change log reads what OrcaSlicer already keeps
124:### Existing command paths are valuable and should be reused
135:### Workspace IDs need explicit project-session scope
148:### Presentation objects must not own model behavior
160:### GUI event-loop delay is not a project-ready signal
175:### History availability depends on which tab is on screen
185:### Undo and redo can silently do nothing
196:### A loaded object is not automatically printable
212:### OrcaSlicer has no printer object; a named printer is a user profile
235:### OrcaSlicer's notifications are read back, not drawn
299:### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners
310:## 3. Resolved implementation problems
312:### Selection events arrived before the duplicate command returned
328:### Adapter selection needed exactly one notification
342:### Rename behavior was embedded in the object-list presentation
357:### Logical transactions are safer than delayed coalescing
373:### A parented top-level shell did not have an independent lifetime
390:### Native choice dismissal moved focus to the opaque shell
404:### One-time window raising did not guarantee continued occlusion
421:### Automatic top-level placement did not ensure visible placement
434:### A borderless shell had no normal recovery action
448:### Unsupported native selection could be mistaken for no selection
460:### Invalid, missing, and stale IDs needed different errors
474:### Sibling widgets and static owners must plan for destruction order
495:### A canvas event posted from a command had not run when the command returned
503:### `Plater::select_object` returns early when the canvas already holds the selection
512:### The object list changes the model without announcing it
518:### Orca gives every loaded object the first filament slot
525:### A plate carries settings only by Orca's own test

### OrcaSlicer's notifications are read back, not drawn

OrcaSlicer reports print problems through three unrelated producers (print
validation in `Plater`, slicing steps on the background thread, plate checks in
`GLCanvas3D`), and results of actions from dozens of call sites. All of them
end in `NotificationManager`. Inside the shell that list is the source of
truth for what JusPrin draws (see "Print issues and OrcaSlicer's
notifications" in the architecture guide). What was learned about it:

- **Three additions to `NotificationManager`, 13 lines in all.**
  `for_each_notification` visits the type, level and current text of every
  notification that is shown. `update_notifications` calls
  `report_notifications_updated()` on its first line. `render_notifications`
  skips its drawing loop while the Prepare canvas has its legacy overlays
  hidden.
- **The observer call is first in `update_notifications`, not last.** That
  function returns early while the application window is not the active one.
  With the call after that return, nothing would be read while the person
  types to an agent in another application. It runs on every idle turn of
  every canvas, so the listener only compares, and rebuilds on a change
  (343 comparisons to 11 rebuilds in one test run).
- **Only the drawing loop is skipped, never the end of
  `render_notifications`.** The end deletes a closed plate warning and records
  the time of the draw. `PlaterWarningNotification::close()` only hides the
  notification and relies on that deletion; a hidden one makes OrcaSlicer
  refuse to push the same words again. An early return from the function left
  such warnings stuck for the session. It asks the Prepare canvas rather than
  the canvas being drawn: Check print is a second canvas whose own flag is
  never set.
- **Hidden means absent.** The accessor leaves out a hidden notification, as
  `get_notification_count()` does. OrcaSlicer hides validation and plate
  warnings while its preview is shown.
- **A notification has no readable target.** The object is captured inside the
  "Jump to" callback. So the object comes from asking the check again:
  `Print::validate` (public, `const`, under a millisecond on small plates, one
  error and one warning at most), `ModelInstance::print_volume_state`,
  `GLCanvas3D::check_volumes_outside_state` with its `ObjectFilamentResults`,
  and `step_state_with_warnings`. A warning's `type` is left uninitialised by
  some producers, so never use it for identity.
- **Slice-result problems are notified late.** `_set_warning_notification_if_needed`
  runs when the preview canvas loads the G-code. Right after a slice the list
  holds none of: path outside the plate, nozzle reach, plate surface. They are
  in `PartPlate::get_slice_result()` at once, and
  `is_slice_result_ready_for_print()` already refuses.
- **A critical slicing failure leaves no notification.** `Plater` shows a
  dialog instead. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED`, which `Plater.cpp` defines and no
  header declares, carries the reason and the object;
  `Workspace/PlaterProjectState.hpp` declares it, and `Plater.cpp` includes
  that header ahead of the definition, so no OrcaSlicer line changes. The
  handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()`.
- **The print lags the project by up to 500 ms.**
  `Plater::is_background_process_update_scheduled()` is true until OrcaSlicer
  applies an edit; until then neither the print nor the notifications describe
  the project as it is. This is what separates "checking" from "no issues".
- **A closed notification returns only with the next real edit.** OrcaSlicer
  validates again when applying an edit changes the print, not when an update
  is merely scheduled.
- **Some plate checks are quieter than they look.** `check_tpu_printable_status`
  returns true unconditionally. The PLA with PETG warning is skipped when the
  printer has a tool change time above zero, which the Bambu Lab H2D profile
  does. A brim is trimmed at the plate edge and at a nozzle's reach; a skirt is
  what puts a path outside.
- **OrcaSlicer validates only the active plate.**

### Application teardown can re-enter destroyed owners

Quitting while model volumes are loaded can crash:
`~GLCanvas3D → reset_volumes → Selection::clear → Plater::canvas3D()` runs
after `Plater::priv` is destroyed and dereferences null. This is inherited
upstream behavior — crash reports with the identical signature predate the
JusPrin shell (2026-08-28) and the stock-mode harness reproduces it with all
fork runtime code inert. Until it is fixed in upstream teardown ordering,
automated GUI scenarios should end on an empty project (`new_project`) before
exiting; both harnesses do.

## 3. Resolved implementation problems
# Printer agents

Printer agents isolate printer-specific communication from the rest of OrcaSlicer. The GUI and
`DeviceManager` operate on a shared set of printer operations and device state; a selected printer
agent implements those operations for a particular printer ecosystem. The agent boundary allows
Bambu, Moonraker-based printers, built-in integrations, and Python-provided integrations to use the
same application workflow without making the GUI understand every printer protocol.

The current boundary is an adapter boundary around the existing application contract. In particular,
some request fields and message payloads still use the Bambu-shaped representation that existing
`MachineObject` and `DeviceManager` code consumes. The printer agent is responsible for translating
that representation into the protocol spoken by its printer. This is an intentional compatibility
constraint of the current design; the interface is not yet a neutral printer protocol.

The v1 dialect migration path is deliberately narrow. `DeviceManager` currently speaks the Bambu JSON
dialect because that is the payload shape already used throughout the command and state workflow. The
v1 `OrcaPrinterAgent` also accepts that Bambu dialect. Its transport path places the small translation
needed for the target printer at `deliver_to_sink`, keeping the compatibility code at the edge rather
than spreading it through `DeviceManager` or the agent interface.

The eventual direction is for `DeviceManager` to produce an Orca JSON dialect. The Bambu agent will then
own the translation from Orca JSON to Bambu's protocol, while `OrcaPrinterAgent` can forward the Orca
payload directly to its sink. The v1 translation at `deliver_to_sink` can then be removed without
changing `DeviceManager`, the command callers, or the rest of the agent workflow.

# OrcaSlicer's messages in the JusPrin view

OrcaSlicer tells the person things in windows: a box with OK, a question, the
"Transfer or discard changes" window, a tip. In the JusPrin view most of those
windows would cover a screen built around the project chat, and many of them
are about pages the view hides. JusPrin takes each such message before its
window opens, keeps the reason it was said, and shows it where the view shows
that kind of news. The code is in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/OrcaMessages/`.

## Where a message is taken

OrcaSlicer speaks in one of two ways.

- It opens a modal window inside the call that decided to speak. Every modal
  window passes wxWidgets' modal hook, where JusPrin's dialog listeners
  already answer the windows a tool call or a file open raises
  (`Workspace/DialogListeners.hpp`). A window no listener answered goes to
  `OrcaMessages::take_modal`, while the code that asked is still on the stack.
- It puts the message off. `GUI::show_error`, `GUI_App::show_dialog` and
  `GUI_App::push_notification` queue the window and return, so by the time it
  opens the reason is gone. One line at the top of each of the three functions
  hands the message over first: `report_error_box` (`Workspace/FileLoads.hpp`),
  `take_app_message` and `take_printer_message`. A fourth line in
  `GUI_App::process_network_msg` notes that what follows is the network
  plug-in's message. The lines reach JusPrin through `JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp`.

Those four lines are the fork's whole footprint in OrcaSlicer's files for this
feature. Each is one neutral statement marked `// JusPrin:`.

## The cause

A message is only as useful as its reason. The reason, a `Cause`, is noted at
the doors where work comes in, by code that knows it:

| Cause | Noted by |
| --- | --- |
| A printer's answer to a connection | `Printers::record_connection_event`, called from OrcaSlicer's connection handler before it opens its box |
| A printer's reply to a command | `take_printer_message`, which `push_notification` gives the printer |
| The network plug-in's message | `plugin_message_cause`, at the top of `process_network_msg` |
| A slice that ended in an error | JusPrin's listener of the finished slice, which runs before OrcaSlicer's |
| A failed upload to a print host | JusPrin's listener of the upload queue's error event |

A cause noted by a listener lasts until the event being handled ends
(`note_cause`); one noted by a scope lasts while the scope does
(`ScopedCause`). A person's click in OrcaSlicer's own menus has no cause.

A cause can say that the code that noted it tells the person itself
(`told_elsewhere`): the print issues tell a failed slice, the upload's entry
in the chat tells a failed upload, and the printer chat tells the answer to a
connection it started and is waiting for
(`Printers::expect_connection_answer`). Such a message is taken and shown
nowhere else, so the person does not read it twice.

## The rule at the hook

For a window no listener answered, while the view is installed:

- A file or folder picker and the chooser of a ZIP's files are the person's and
  open as OrcaSlicer's. A listener of a file the person opens themself shows
  them too, rather than cancelling them.
- A window with fields, and a question with more than one answer, are the
  person's and open.
- A message with only OK is taken, unless another window is open over the main
  one, such as OrcaSlicer's settings window or Preferences, and the message has
  no cause. The box then belongs with that window, where the person is
  looking.
- "Transfer or discard changes", and the "unsaved changes" question OrcaSlicer
  asks before it reloads profiles (`check_and_save_current_preset_changes`,
  `check_and_keep_current_preset_changes`), are answered after a version of
  the project is saved to its history: the setting changes are dropped and
  the version keeps them. The person never chooses between saving and
  discarding; version history is the way back. If no version can be saved,
  the window is cancelled, so nothing changes, and the failure is reported as
  an unexpected error.
- The same window class asks whether to copy one nozzle's settings to the
  other on a two-nozzle printer (`Tab::sync_excluder`). That is a question
  about a copy and stays the person's. OrcaSlicer tells the three uses apart
  only by their titles, so JusPrin compares the titles as OrcaSlicer builds
  them.
- A tip window is taken.
- JusPrin's own windows are never taken. They open through
  `OrcaMessages/OwnDialogs.hpp` (`show_own_modal`, `show_own_message`,
  `show_own_error`), which marks them as JusPrin's while they are shown.

The view also refuses a switch of the main window to any page other than Home,
Prepare and Project (`ShellController::on_notebook_page_changing`), so code
that jumps to OrcaSlicer's Device page, or the key that steps through its
pages, leaves the person where they are.

## Where a taken message is shown

`OrcaMessages/MessageRoutes.hpp` decides, from the message and its cause:

- A message about a printer, a connection's answer or a command's reply:
  an entry in the project chat, the kind the app's own work leaves there
  (`Agent::AgentHost::begin_work`), titled with the printer's name as JusPrin
  names it, marked failed and carrying OrcaSlicer's words. The chat pane opens
  for it. The entry is saved with the project, so a message that arrives while
  the person is on Home is there when they return.
- A message told elsewhere: nothing more.
- Any other message: a confirmation on the canvas, where OrcaSlicer's own
  notices of an action's outcome are drawn.
- An answered unsaved-changes question, a tip, a refused page switch:
  nothing more.

The words are OrcaSlicer's, unchanged and translated by its catalogs.

## Testing

`JusPrinShellHarness --orca-messages <dir>` makes OrcaSlicer speak through
its real code in each of these ways and checks which window opened, what was
taken with which cause, and where it was shown. `--classic-messages` turns the
taking off while the view stays installed (`set_taking_for_tests`), so the same
run shows OrcaSlicer's windows as the classic view does. Every harness mode
fails its run if, while the view takes messages, an OrcaSlicer message with
only OK or an unsaved-changes question reached the person, or a printer
message was taken without its printer.

OrcaSlicer opens message windows from hundreds of call sites. The JusPrin

- **A window put off has lost its reason by the time it opens.**
  `GUI::show_error`, `GUI_App::show_dialog` and `GUI_App::push_notification`

  with no caller on the stack. The message is taken at the top of each of the

  once is taken at the hook.
- **The reason has to be noted at the source.** A box's words do not say what
  it is about: "Connect ... failed!" names no device id, and the network
  plug-in's update message names none at all. The cause is noted by the code
  that knows it, and JusPrin's listeners of a finished slice or a failed
  upload run before OrcaSlicer's own, since the handler bound later runs
  first.
- **One window class has three uses.** `UnsavedChangesDialog` asks
  "Transfer or discard changes" on a profile switch, "<caption>: unsaved
  changes" before profiles are reloaded, and whether to copy one nozzle's
  settings to the other. The copy always has unsaved options, so the dirty

  "remember my choice" set it returns the remembered action before the modal

  `Tab::select_preset` drop the outgoing edits itself; the reload callers read

- **A failed upload's entry reads done.** The upload's chat entry follows
  OrcaSlicer's progress notification and is finished as done when the
  notification goes away (`PrintIssues/WorkFeed.cpp`). Its failure is in the
  upload queue's error event, not in the notification's disappearance.

'''

result.output:
**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.

**How.** In a worktree on a new branch from `jusprin-dev`, the development branch:

```bash
git rev-parse <new release>^{commit} > "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/MERGE_HEAD"
git merge-recursive <last release taken> -- HEAD <new release>
```

Resolve the conflicts, then `git commit`. A later patch release on the same release branch, such as 2.5.1 after 2.5.0, needs no override: a plain `git merge` finds the right base.

**The test.** Is the merge base the release we last took, and not a commit on upstream's development line?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main` or `git merge v2.5.0` with no base given. Each produces thousands of conflicts in files JusPrin never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<last release taken> <newest upstream release> HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

input.content:
JusPrin view takes OrcaSlicer's message windows and shows them in place

In the JusPrin view, OrcaSlicer still opened its own windows: a box with
only OK when a printer refused a print job, "Transfer or discard changes"
when a profile was switched with edits, a tip, or a jump to the hidden
Device page. Those windows covered the chat-centred screen and often spoke
about pages the view hides.

JusPrin now takes each such message before its window opens, keeps the
reason it was said, and shows it where the view shows that kind of news:

- A printer's message (a connection answer or a command reply) becomes a
  failed entry in the project chat, titled with the printer's name as
  JusPrin names it. It is saved with the project, so a message that comes
  while the person is on Home is there when they return.
- A message the print issues or the printer chat already tells (a failed
  slice, an answer the printer chat waits for) is not shown twice.
- Any other message with only OK becomes a confirmation on the canvas.
- Pickers, the ZIP chooser, questions and windows with fields stay the
  person's. A message with no cause stays OrcaSlicer's box when another
  window (the settings window, Preferences) is open over the main one.
- "Transfer or discard changes" and the "unsaved changes" question asked
  before profiles reload are answered after a version of the project is
  saved: the setting changes are dropped and the version keeps them. If no
  version can be saved, the window is cancelled, nothing changes, and the
  failure is reported as an unexpected error. The same window class asks
  whether to copy one nozzle's settings to the other; that stays a
  question.
- The main window refuses a switch to any page but Home, Prepare and
  Project.
- JusPrin's own windows open through OrcaMessages/OwnDialogs.hpp and are
  never taken.

The code is in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/OrcaMessages/. OrcaSlicer's files
change by four lines, each marked "// JusPrin:" and reached through
OrcaHooks.hpp: GUI::show_error, GUI_App::show_dialog,
GUI_App::push_notification and GUI_App::process_network_msg. In
GUI::show_error the existing fork line now calls report_error_box, which
still hands a file load's error to the file load first. A rebase
simulated with git merge-tree against v2.5.1 and against upstream/main
(4f71398a0f) conflicts in the same files with and without this change.

Tests: JusPrinShellHarness --orca-messages <dir> makes OrcaSlicer speak
through its real code in each of these ways and checks which window
opened, what was taken with which cause, and where it was shown.
--classic-messages runs the same cases with taking off and expects
OrcaSlicer's windows. Every harness mode now fails if an OK-only message
or an unsaved-changes question reached the person, or a printer message
was taken without its printer. The printer-menu mode checks a printer
switch with unsaved edits, including a failed save; the printer-setup
mode checks failed Bambu connections show no OrcaSlicer box.
dialog_slice_error_after_the_call now expects the slice error box not to
open over the chat.

Not agreed yet, built as defaults: setting changes are dropped after a
version is saved; every page but Home, Prepare and Project is refused; a
message with no cause becomes a canvas confirmation; a failed save
cancels the switch and reports an unexpected error.

Design: docs/HLSD/orca-messages.md. Lesson:
agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md.
